title: Materialize Git LFS bytes
responsibility: Recognize Git LFS pointers and download content only from permitted HTTPS locations with matching size and hash.

inputs.name: githubLfs.options
inputs.description: The GitHub repository identity and access configuration used for an LFS pointer: repository owner, name, ID and installation ID build the batch endpoint and token scope, and the token callback supplies a contents-read installation token. The optional fetch implementation replaces global fetch for both requests; otherwise global fetch is used.

inputs.name: githubLfs.bytes
inputs.description: The raw repository blob bytes to inspect; bytes not starting with `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/` are returned unchanged. If that prefix is present, the bytes must decode to the exact v1 pointer form with a lowercase 64-character SHA-256 and canonical decimal size, with an optional final newline; the size must be a safe integer no greater than 50,000,000.

outputs.name: githubLfs
outputs.description: The resolved value is the same input bytes when they are not an LFS pointer, or the downloaded object bytes after a pointer is recognized. Pointer bytes are returned only when their length matches the declared size and their SHA-256 matches the OID; the declared size is capped at 50,000,000, and the download URL must be credential-free HTTPS on githubusercontent.com or github-cloud.s3.amazonaws.com (including subdomains), with no explicit port.

errors.name: CollaborationInputError
errors.description: Malformed prefixed pointers and declarations above the size limit are rejected directly as invalid-lfs-pointer or lfs-size-limit. Failures during token acquisition, batch parsing, URL validation, download, response handling or integrity checking are caught and rejected as lfs-unavailable.
